newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close higher as weather eyed.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close higher as weather eyed.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures closed strongly higher, especially soymeal, with outlooks for cool weather to soon move into the U.S. Midwest the catalyst for the rally, traders said.
Products followed a surge in soybeans with fund buying triggering the gains, they said.
"The potential for some cool weather got this market excited along with the decline in crop conditions," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Tight cash markets, active exports and firm meal basis values lent support.
A lack of soymeal deliveries also gave that market support with persistent heavy deliveries on soyoil limiting gains in that pit.
Traders said there was talk China may buy 500,000 tonnes of soymeal by the end of the year.
Fund buying in soymeal totaled at least 2,500 lots, the traders said.
Soymeal closed $4.80 to $6.80 per ton higher, with September up $5.80 at $272.60. Soyoil closed 0.23 to 0.30 cent per lb higher, with September up 0.28 at 25.68 cents.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 24,000, up from 15,167 Monday, according to the CBOT. Soymeal options volume was estimated at 2,800, up from 1,832 Monday.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 18,000, down from 18,174 Monday. Soyoil options volume was estimated at 500, up from 263 Monday, CBOT said.
